A DOG DAYCARE. YOUR FRIENDS. ONE MOP.

Kennel Chaos is a co-op simulator about being the people who actually do the work. No staff menu, no spreadsheet. You're the one holding the scoop. Bring your friends, split the jobs, and watch the plan survive roughly ten minutes.

THE DOGS ARE THE CHALLENGE

Twenty-one breeds. Every dog is a unique challenge:

· The Escape Artist is testing every gate right now. She will find the one you forgot.

· The Sneaky Pooper waits until you're facing the other way, and picks a corner.

· The Shaker waits until it's out of the tub and next to you.

· Zoomies doesn't care what's in the way, including you.

· Rolls In It has already found the mess you were about to clean.

· The Poop Eater solves that problem in the worst possible way.

YOU CAN CARRY ONE THING

A dog, or a tool. Never both. Tools live on the racks you bought and put somewhere. So "somewhere" turns out to be a decision you'll think about a lot, usually while jogging back across the building holding a wriggling beagle.

SMALL PROBLEMS COMPOUND

A fresh poop takes two seconds to scoop. Ignore it and somebody walks through it. Now there are paw prints down the corridor. Ignore those and they dry, and dried needs a scrub. This is how a nice afternoon becomes a Code Brown.

BUILD THE PLACE FIRST

Start with an empty building and a small pile of money. Buy runs, tubs, grooming tables, food prep, play equipment. Paint the walls. Hang wallpaper. Put a clock up. Then open the doors and find out which of your decisions were stupid.

RUN THE PET SHOP TOO

Your daycare has a store. Order stock by the carton, carry it in from the delivery door and fill the shelves by hand. Lay out your own shop floor with gondolas, a food shelf, a chiller, an apparel table and a cat shelf. Customers come in with their own shopping lists and moods. Some want one thing, some fill a basket, and some walk out if the price is too high. Set your prices, scan every item at the till and keep the line moving. Each night you see the sales you missed because a shelf was empty, and Cozy Kennel sends a shoplifter to test you.

THEN PAY FOR ALL OF IT

Takings in, upkeep out, stars up or down depending on whether every dog actually got what its care card promised. Spend what's left before bed. Do it again tomorrow, but with more dogs.

FEATURES

· 1–8 player online co-op. It is significantly funnier with friends

· 21 dog breeds with traits that genuinely change your day

· A mess system with actual consequences: fresh, stepped in, tracked, dried

· Build and decorate your own daycare, room by room

· First-person, hands-on, no menus doing the work for you

· Dogs that are extremely good and extremely bad at the same time

WHO MADE THIS

Kennel Chaos is made by a solo developer with 12 years in game development, whose previous game passed 1 million downloads.

Kepler-186e, 9 November 1989. The Kaiserreich has landed. Nobody asked the planet.

Ash plains, spore fields, lava rifts. What began as an expedition is now a colony fighting for its next week. Water is scarce, Flux power is precious, and beneath the surface the Ordo Arachnis stirs: a swarm that does not see the colonists as guests, but as something to be removed.

Kepler Protocol is turn-based strategy about hard survival, played week by week. Every week counts, every soldier counts. A careless commander will not last long.

A world with height. The world map is a tilted 3D landscape. Ridges block sight, slopes slow columns, rifts become choke points. What you do stays on the map: roads, construction sites, tracks, scorched ground, graves.

Supply is a front of its own. Find water, tap Flux veins, build roads and keep the columns moving. A colony without supply starves long before the swarm arrives. Far ahead waits the Kaiserreich's great goal: the planetary core drill.

An enemy with no commander. The Ordo Arachnis follows no orders, only chemistry: a pheromone field that every brood follows on its own. Nobody decides, yet the swarm flows like an army ant raid. It grows first, then it bites. The heavy castes appear only when the hive is large enough.

Every loss has weight. The dead and the wounded are not the same, and morale breaks before the line does. Battles are fought out on the spot, and you watch them unfold.

War as it was fought. The Kaiserreich fights like an army of 1917 that ended up on a foreign planet. Field guns are drawn by horse teams, limbered and unlimbered, and stand behind the infantry line. A shell takes longer the farther it flies, and every bullet travels from the muzzle to where it lands. Each soldier takes cover behind what really stands in the line of fire. Trenches are dug by the men who hold them, and they stay.

A world with physics. Every week has its wind. It drives fire across the spore fields, carries spore clouds and pushes the smoke of battle into your line of sight. Set a fire with the wind and the field burns down fast; against a strong wind the flames will not jump at all.

Dark science fiction. A distant empire, gas masks in the open, violet-black grass under a foreign sun. No heroic poses. Just a colony trying to see another week.

Features
  • Turn-based strategy, week by week, on a tilted 3D world map with height, line of sight and fog of war
  • Hard survival: water, food, Flux power and supply decide whether the colony lives
  • A swarm with no commander: enemy behaviour that emerges from a pheromone field
  • The swarm matures: first it grows, then the heavy castes arrive
  • Visible work: construction sites, columns, tracks and scars stay on the map
  • Battles fought out on the spot, with dead, wounded and broken morale
  • Fought like 1917: horse-drawn guns, trenches, cover behind what stands in the line of fire
  • A wind every week: fire, spore clouds and battle smoke drift with it
  • Distinct maps, each with its own terrain and its own dangers
  • Dark sci-fi atmosphere with its own music and soundscape
Made by a single developer. Early Access means you play now and help shape what comes next.

A tiny monkey that types along with you.

Keyboard Companion puts a little pixel monkey at the bottom of your screen. He sits behind his own keyboard, and whenever you type, he types too. In whatever app you're using, all day long.

He has a life of his own

Stop typing for a moment and he gets busy: he peels a banana, scratches his head, looks around, yawns, and eventually nods off. Press a key and he wakes right up, a little startled, and gets back to work.

Every key you press, he presses too

The exact key you hit lights up on his keyboard and a little keycap pops into the air. Type long enough and his tongue sneaks out in concentration.

Stays out of your way

  • Sits on top of your other windows without stealing focus. Clicks go straight through to what's behind him

  • Drag him anywhere and scale him to any size you like

  • Lightweight, made to run all day while you work, write, chat or play

Your keystrokes stay yours

Keyboard Companion never records what you type. No words, no text, no order of keys, nothing is sent anywhere. It only counts how many keys you press per day, and that count stays on your computer. The "light up keys" effect can be turned off when you share your screen.

Keyboard Curse is a chaotic 2D rage-platformer where your keyboard is both your controller and your biggest enemy.

Every time you press a key, a matching keycap appears inside the level. Press A, D, or W, and those buttons become real objects that can help you reach the goal… or completely ruin your run.

Jump too much, and the level fills with W keycaps.
Move carelessly, and you may trap yourself with your own inputs.
Panic, and the curse only gets stronger.

Your goal is simple: reach the end of each level using skill, timing, and as few inputs as possible.

Keycap Co is a management game about running a keyboard shop and starting your own keyboard brand. Begin with a small store and a few shelves. Choose your stock, set your prices, and use the profits to expand.

Run the shop

Order keyboards from different suppliers, from budget office models to expensive custom builds. Your customers have different budgets and preferences. Find out what they want, decide what to stock, and adjust prices when boards aren’t selling.

Hire staff to help customers, work the checkout, and keep the shelves full. Plan the shop layout, add furniture and decorations, and move into larger stores as the business grows.

Design your own keyboards

Start your own brand and choose the cases, switches, keycaps, and features for your keyboards. Research new options, pay for production, and launch your designs.

Sell them in your shop and fill wholesale orders. Read the press reviews to see what people liked, what they disliked, and what you could change for your next release.

See what customers think

Customers leave reviews based on their visits. They might thank the employee who helped them, complain about the price, or mention a keyboard they couldn’t find. Use their feedback to improve the shop.

Hear the keyboards

Listen as customers test keyboards around the shop, with different sounds for linear, tactile, clicky, and silent switches.

Skip the lengthy character creation and focus on the fun of combat!

Kick the Dungeon is a card-based tactical roguelike game that uses the SRD 5.1 rules. Assemble your unique party, craft your own build, and enjoy the thrill of battle. Use cards to unleash familiar spells like Fireball and Magic Missile — every run offers a completely different experience.



Kick The Dungeon is a turn-based tactical RPG inspired by DND 5E-style combat. Build your party, enter dangerous battle maps, and defeat a wide variety of enemies through positioning, skill timing, equipment choices, and team composition.

The game focuses on tactical combat progression. You choose from multiple class-based characters, form a party, and fight through different regions and battle stages filled with goblins, beasts, undead, constructs, and other enemies. Every battle is shaped by initiative order, movement range, attack distance, skill area, armor class, damage rolls, and saving throws. Victory depends not only on raw damage, but also on positioning, target priority, and smart use of each turn.

The current version includes 6 playable class templates, such as Fighter, Wizard, Rogue, Ranger, Cleric, Paladin, Each class offers a different combat role and playstyle, including frontline defense, ranged attacks, spellcasting, healing, burst damage, and mobility. Choosing the right team setup has a major impact on how each encounter plays out.

The game currently features 200+ skill entries, 90+ monsters, 50+ pieces of equipment, and 30 battle stages across multiple regions. Players will explore battlefields such as forests, mazes, scorched lands, and towers, facing different enemy groups, elite encounters, and large creatures. Terrain, enemy combinations, and party composition all create different tactical challenges.

Combat is built around clear turn phases. Each unit acts according to initiative and uses movement, actions, bonus actions, and reactions to influence the battlefield. You will need to balance melee attacks, ranged damage, spells, healing, buffs, and debuffs while adapting to the changing situation of each fight. Area attacks, single-target burst, status effects, and reaction-based mechanics can all turn the tide of battle.

If you enjoy turn-based strategy, party-building, grid-based tactics, and fantasy combat inspired by tabletop mechanics, Kick The Dungeon offers a combat-focused experience built around planning, execution, and satisfying tactical victories.

A horror streamer dies.

She wakes up again.

Every death reveals something new.

And the person closest to her may be part of the reason.

What begins as a beautiful fantasy slowly becomes a waking nightmare.

Haru, a horror streamer, awakens in a mysterious world that should not exist. Beneath a sky filled with unfamiliar stars, she meets Elinia—a gentle, mysterious girl who seems to know more than she says. Together, they search for a way home through moonlit gardens, silent halls, and flowers that seem to watch from the darkness.

But something is wrong.

The air carries the unmistakable scent of blood. Familiar rooms change the moment Haru looks away. Every death refuses to end the story.

Instead, it returns Haru to the same day with new memories, new wounds, and another fragment of the truth. The closer Haru gets to Elinia, the more this beautiful world reveals its cruel rules.

Is Elinia trapped in this loop too?

Or is she the reason it exists?

Your choices shape Haru's path through a branching psychological horror story. Trust Elinia, question her, protect her, or push her away. Every decision changes what you discover, which memories survive, and what awaits at the end of the loop.

Uncover hidden scenes, revisit key moments with new knowledge, and piece together the truth behind the loop—where comfort and terror become impossible to separate.

Will you save Elinia...

Or will you become trapped in the same day forever?

A story where every ending is only the beginning.

Welcome to Kintsugi Cottage

Kintsugi Cottage is a cozy cleanup-restoration game set in a small village museum. Search through the rubble, and restore every artifact.

A cottage full of galleries

Each gallery has a unique set of artifacts, referencing a specific historic style. Learn all the patterns, colors, and materials during your time at the cottage.

So much to restore

  • 70+ artifacts to restore in the full game

  • 1000+ pieces to find and fit back together

  • 15 genres of artifact, drawn from several historic times

Take your time

No timers, no scores, no pressure. This is a relaxing cozy game, think of it as a 3D jigsaw puzzle.

Unless of course you're interested in the speedrun achievements...
